_meta.purpose: The deterministic fix catalog (WS-5). Rule ID -> concrete Terraform change. No LLM in this path.
_meta.governance: Static, checked-in, human-reviewed data -- the same rule as rule-severity.json and control-map.json. The model never writes a fix rule at runtime.
_meta.prioritization: Strictly by measured corpus frequency across tests/fixtures/tf-0*. 30 rules = 119/158 findings (75%) of the corpus, and 119/139 (86%) of everything that is deterministically fixable at all.

notDeterministicallyFixable.CKV_AWS_355: IAM wildcard resource. There is no correct set of ARNs to narrow to without knowing intent -- routed to the LLM path (WS-6). Never auto-applicable either way.
notDeterministicallyFixable.CKV_AWS_290: Same. IAM write access without constraints.
notDeterministicallyFixable.CKV_AWS_117: Lambda in a VPC. Choosing subnets/SGs is an architecture decision; synthesising an empty VPC would cut the function off from its dependencies. Routed to the LLM path.

_meta.autoApplicable: autoApplicable=true is the catalog's human-reviewed opinion, and it is only ever a NOMINATION. patch_terraform.auto_apply_blocker() can veto it and there is no path by which a never-list category becomes auto-applicable. See SPEC §6.3.

CKV_AWS_338.title: CloudWatch log group retains logs for at least 1 year
CKV_AWS_338.rationale: Single attribute, additive, no access impact. When the existing value is an expression (var.log_retention_days) this degrades to a modify and the engine forces it diff-only -- overriding a deliberate parameterisation is not unambiguous.

changes.name: retention_in_days
changes.description: retain CloudWatch logs for 365 days

CKV_AWS_158.title: CloudWatch log group is encrypted by KMS
CKV_AWS_158.rationale: Creates a KMS key AND its key policy. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list: a wrong key policy bricks log delivery, and re-keying an existing log group is not reversible in place.

changes.name: kms_key_id
changes.description: encrypt the log group with a customer-managed KMS key

CKV2_AWS_62.title: S3 bucket has event notifications enabled
CKV2_AWS_62.rationale: A single additive companion that routes bucket events to EventBridge. It grants nothing, denies nothing, and cannot break access.

changes.description: send S3 events for ${name} to EventBridge

CKV_AWS_18.title: S3 bucket has access logging enabled
CKV_AWS_18.rationale: Creates a new destination bucket. Which bucket receives access logs is an operational decision (most orgs have a central one), so a human picks.

changes.description: enable S3 server access logging for ${name}

CKV_AWS_144.title: S3 bucket has cross-region replication enabled
CKV_AWS_144.rationale: Creates a destination bucket AND an IAM role. Real cross-region replication also needs an aliased provider in a second region, which only a human can decide. Diff-only, always.

changes.description: enable versioning on ${name} (a hard prerequisite for replication)
replicate ${name} to a second bucket

CKV_AWS_130.title: VPC subnets do not assign a public IP by default
CKV_AWS_130.rationale: Access-affecting. Instances launched into a public subnet stop getting public IPs; anything reachable that way goes dark. A human decides whether the subnet is meant to be public.

changes.name: map_public_ip_on_launch
changes.description: stop auto-assigning public IPs in this subnet

CKV_AWS_116.title: Lambda function has a dead-letter queue
CKV_AWS_116.rationale: Creates an SQS queue and requires an execution-role grant the patch does not add. Diff-only so the reviewer sees the missing IAM half.

changes.name: dead_letter_config
changes.description: send failed async invocations of ${name} to a DLQ

CKV_AWS_173.title: Lambda environment variables are encrypted with a CMK
CKV_AWS_173.rationale: Creates a KMS key. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list.

changes.name: kms_key_arn
changes.description: encrypt ${name}'s environment variables with a CMK

CKV_AWS_272.title: Lambda function validates code signing
CKV_AWS_272.rationale: Enforcing code signing REJECTS every unsigned deployment. Turning that on without a signing pipeline in place breaks the next deploy.

changes.name: code_signing_config_arn
changes.description: require signed artifacts for ${name}

CKV_AWS_115.title: Lambda function has a concurrent-execution limit
CKV_AWS_115.rationale: The correct reservation is workload-specific. A guessed limit throttles production traffic, so this is not semantically unambiguous and never auto-applies.

changes.name: reserved_concurrent_executions
changes.description: cap concurrency for ${name} (TUNE THIS -- 100 is a placeholder)

CKV2_AWS_53.title: API Gateway request is validated
CKV2_AWS_53.rationale: Turning on request validation starts rejecting requests that previously succeeded. Behaviour-changing, so a human confirms.

changes.description: add a request validator for ${name}

changes.name: request_validator_id
changes.description: validate requests to ${name}

CKV_AWS_260.title: Security group does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 80
CKV_AWS_260.rationale: CATEGORY 1 ON THE HARD NEVER-AUTO-APPLY LIST. Narrowing an SG CIDR is how you lock an operator (or every customer) out of production. The diff is generated; a human applies it, having first set the variable to a range that is actually correct.

changes.name: cidr_ipv4
changes.description: narrow ${name} from the whole internet to a trusted CIDR

CKV_AWS_195.title: Glue component has a security configuration
CKV_AWS_195.rationale: Creates a KMS key. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list.

changes.name: security_configuration
changes.description: attach an encrypting security configuration to ${name}

CKV_AWS_300.title: S3 lifecycle configuration aborts failed multipart uploads
CKV_AWS_300.rationale: Additive lifecycle rule. Deletes nothing a caller can see -- only incomplete multipart uploads, which are unreadable by definition. No access impact.

changes.name: rule
changes.description: abort incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days

CKV_AWS_145.title: S3 bucket is encrypted with KMS by default
CKV_AWS_145.rationale: Creates a KMS key. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list. Also re-keys an existing bucket: old objects stay under the old key and every reader needs kms:Decrypt.

changes.name: rule
changes.description: switch ${name} from AES256 to a customer-managed KMS key
add KMS default encryption to ${name}

CKV_AWS_21.title: S3 bucket has versioning enabled
CKV_AWS_21.rationale: SPEC §6.3 names versioning as an auto-apply example. Additive, unambiguous, cannot break access. If a versioning resource already exists and is Suspended, the fix becomes a modify and the engine forces it diff-only.

changes.description: enable versioning on ${name}

changes.name: versioning_configuration
changes.description: switch versioning on for ${name}

CKV_AWS_163.title: ECR image scanning on push is enabled
CKV_AWS_163.rationale: Additive, in-place, unambiguous. Scanning an image cannot deny a pull.

changes.name: scan_on_push
changes.description: scan ${name} images on push

changes.name: image_scanning_configuration
changes.description: scan ${name} images on push

CKV_AWS_136.title: ECR repository is encrypted with KMS
CKV_AWS_136.rationale: encryption_configuration forces REPLACEMENT of the repository, which destroys every image in it. Never auto-applied despite being a single additive block.

changes.name: encryption_type
changes.description: encrypt ${name} with KMS (WARNING: forces repository replacement)

changes.name: encryption_configuration
changes.description: encrypt ${name} with KMS (WARNING: forces repository replacement)

CKV_AWS_51.title: ECR image tags are immutable
CKV_AWS_51.rationale: Immutable tags break any CI job that re-pushes a moving tag (`:latest`). The next pipeline run fails. A human confirms the pipeline is ready.

changes.name: image_tag_mutability
changes.description: make ${name} image tags immutable

CKV_AWS_150.title: Load balancer has deletion protection enabled
CKV_AWS_150.rationale: Single attribute, in-place, cannot break traffic. It only makes an accidental `destroy` fail, which is the point.

changes.name: enable_deletion_protection
changes.description: protect ${name} from accidental deletion

CKV_AWS_131.title: ALB drops invalid HTTP headers
CKV_AWS_131.rationale: Additive, in-place. Drops malformed headers only -- a request smuggling defence, not an access control.

changes.name: drop_invalid_header_fields
changes.description: drop invalid HTTP headers at ${name}

CKV_AWS_2.title: ALB listener uses HTTPS
CKV_AWS_2.rationale: Replaces the listener's default_action. Every plain-HTTP client starts getting a 301. Access-affecting, so diff-only.

changes.name: default_action
changes.description: redirect ${name} from HTTP to HTTPS

CKV_AWS_103.title: Load balancer uses at least TLS 1.2
CKV_AWS_103.rationale: Satisfied by the same HTTP->HTTPS redirect as CKV_AWS_2 (the graph check passes a listener whose default_action redirects to HTTPS). Access-affecting.

changes.name: default_action
changes.description: redirect ${name} to HTTPS so no plaintext listener remains

CKV2_AWS_20.title: ALB redirects HTTP requests into HTTPS
CKV2_AWS_20.rationale: Reported on the aws_lb, fixed on its port-80 HTTP listener -- the linkTo `match` picks that listener specifically and not the HTTPS one. Access-affecting.

changes.name: default_action
changes.description: redirect the HTTP listener of ${name} to HTTPS

CKV_AWS_378.title: Load balancer target group does not use HTTP
CKV_AWS_378.rationale: Switching the target-group protocol to HTTPS means the targets must actually terminate TLS on that port and the health check follows. Break-the-service potential, so diff-only.

changes.name: protocol
changes.description: use HTTPS to reach the targets of ${name} (the targets must serve TLS on this port)

CKV2_AWS_12.title: Default security group of every VPC restricts all traffic
CKV2_AWS_12.rationale: CATEGORY 1 ON THE HARD NEVER-AUTO-APPLY LIST. Adopting the default SG into Terraform strips every rule AWS put there; anything silently relying on it loses connectivity at the next apply.

changes.description: adopt and empty the default security group of ${name}
template: # Added by iac-tools: adopts the VPC's default security group and
# removes every rule from it. Anything currently relying on the default SG
# WILL LOSE CONNECTIVITY. Check before applying.

CKV2_AWS_28.title: Public-facing ALB is protected by WAF
CKV2_AWS_28.rationale: A managed rule group in block mode can reject legitimate traffic on day one. Diff-only, and the template says to run it in count mode first.

changes.description: put ${name} behind the WAF

CKV_AWS_26.title: SNS topic is encrypted
CKV_AWS_26.rationale: Creates a KMS key. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list -- and every existing publisher needs kms:GenerateDataKey on it or publishing starts failing.

changes.name: kms_master_key_id
changes.description: encrypt ${name} at rest with a CMK

CKV_AWS_316.title: CodeBuild project does not run in privileged mode
CKV_AWS_316.rationale: Privileged mode is what lets a build run Docker. Turning it off breaks every docker-build pipeline that needs it. A human confirms.

changes.name: privileged_mode
changes.description: drop privileged mode from ${name} (breaks in-build Docker)

CKV_AWS_147.title: CodeBuild project is encrypted with a CMK
CKV_AWS_147.rationale: Creates a KMS key. Category 4 on the never-auto-apply list.

changes.name: encryption_key
changes.description: encrypt ${name} build artifacts with a CMK
